roll out a patch version that cleans up that issue.

From the error message, it appears that the entire
right hand-side of the assignment evaluates to a matrix
whereas the left-hand side variable mu[n,1] is scalar.

a scalar, Stan does promotion so that (a + c) is a matrix.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] My model does not parse (Maybe a problem in the definition of the parameters?)
parts:
Here's your problem:

mu[n,1] : real

Y[n-1] : (column) vector

B12 : (column) vector

B12' : row vector

Y[n-1] * B12' : matrix

You can't assign a matrix to a real.

Maybe you wanted

B12' * Y[n-1]

instead, which produces a scalar rather than a matrix.
You can also just use:

dot(B12,Y[n-1])

for a dot product, which is a bit more efficient because
it doesn't construct the transposed matrix as an intermediate
step.

The error message, while not indicating the right line
in version 1.0.3, did explain what the error was.

You also have the same problem in the next two terms after the
first one that causes the parsing error.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] My model does not parse (Maybe a problem in the definition of the parameters?)
parts:
It is confusing because

C++/Java: 0-indexed, row-major
R/BUGS: 1-indexed, column-major

Our data types are all described very thoroughly
in the manual. Matrices are matrices, vectors
are column vectors unless declared as row_vector.
If you have a matrix a, then a[2] is a row vector (which
I'm told is very confusing whether you're used to MATLAB
or R -- it seemed natural enough to me coming from
a more functional programming perspective).

We also reduce result types. So that if x is
a row vector and y is a column vector, then
x*y is a real type, not a 1 x 1 vector. And unlike
R, these types don't auto-coerce everywhere.

And we promote argument types. So that if you add
a scalar and a vector, the scalar is treated like
a vector with the scalar in each position.

In the multi_normal distribution, we allow either
a row vector or column vector for the mean (I was
overruled on type checking there because the other
developers liked the flexibility and argued it'd
be less confusing to users to not have to always
make the vector a column vector).

- Bob

El lunes, 12 de noviembre de 2012 17:52:10 UTC-5, Bob Carpenter escribió:
Sorry about the bad error messages.  We're about to
roll out a patch version that cleans up that issue.

 From the error message, it appears that the entire
right hand-side of the assignment evaluates to a matrix
whereas the left-hand side variable mu[n,1] is scalar.

If B12 is a matrix, and Y[n-2] is a scalar, then
Y[n-2]*B12' is a matrix.  If a is a matrix and c is
a scalar, Stan does promotion so that (a + c) is a matrix.

- Bob
